title: SHM with calculus and physical pendulum
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Physics C: Mechanics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: O05-calc-1#t4 term and clue written for the game; O05-calc-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; O05-calc-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; O05-calc-1#t2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: O05-calc-1#N.3, O05-calc-1#N.4, O05-calc-1#N.7, O05-calc-1#N.9, O05-calc-1#N.13a.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Torsion constant
items.clue: Symbol k, in N m per rad: restoring torque of a wire divided by its twist.

items.label: Torsion pendulum
items.clue: Flat object hung horizontally from a wire through its middle, twisted and then released.

items.label: Physical pendulum
items.clue: Rigid body swinging about a fixed axis under gravity, treated using its I about the pivot.

items.label: Simple pendulum
items.clue: Special case with I = mL² and d = L for string length L, so the period depends only on L and g.

questions.stem: A particle of mass m moves along the x-axis. The only force exerted on it is a conservative force for which the system's potential energy is U(x) = βx², where β is a positive constant. Applying Newton's second law gives an equation of the form d²x/dt² = −ω²x. What is the period T of the motion?
The position of an object in SHM is x = A cos(ωt + φ). At t = 0 the object is at x = +A/2 and is moving in the +x direction. What is φ?

A uniform disk of radius R = 0.10 m hangs from a fixed horizontal axle that passes through a point on its rim, perpendicular to the face of the disk. The rotational inertia of a uniform disk of mass M about an axis through its center, perpendicular to its face, is (1/2)MR². The disk is displaced through a small angle and released. What is the period of its oscillations? Use g = 10 m/s².

A torsion pendulum consists of a horizontal uniform disk suspended from a vertical wire attached to its center. The disk undergoes small rotational oscillations about the wire, for which Iα = −kΔθ. Which single change would increase the period of the oscillations?

options.text: Replacing the disk with a thin ring of equal mass and radius
Twisting the disk through a larger angle before it is released
Taking the apparatus to a location where the value of g is smaller
Replacing the disk with a heavier one of the same rotational inertia

questions.stem: A pendulum consists of a light rigid rod of length L, pivoted about a fixed horizontal axis through its upper end, with two small objects, each of mass m, fastened to it: one at a distance L/4 from the axis and one at the rod's lower end. For small angular displacements θ, the small-angle approximation and Newton's second law in rotational form give d²θ/dt² = −ω²θ. What is ω? g is the acceleration due to gravity.
